namespace_vocabulary_note: Each <namespace>: token is spelled in a vocabulary owned by that namespace's maintainer (KISS-CLASSIFY-6.8-0004), versioned independently of this artifact. These are the versions the tokens below were GENERATED AGAINST; a consumer asserting a vocabulary version (KISS-CLASSIFY-6.8-0009) asserts against these. The generator FAILS rather than emit a token whose vocabulary version it cannot state.
dtype_axis_note: recognition_set is all 24 tokens a reader MUST recognize on parse (reserved ones typed-decline, distinct from unknown); usable_set is the 22 a byte-match runs over. The two are different obligations (KISS-CLASSIFY-6.1-0001).
target_axis_note: Each positive vector names the `target` capability token it requires and its `target_namespace`. A consumer implementing only some namespaces/architectures scopes the rest as capability EXCLUSIONS (conformant, KISS-CLASSIFY-6.8), never mismatches — on BOTH sub-axes: namespace (cuda vs vulkan) and capability/arch (sm89 vs sm90). With these tags a consumer reports N/N on the vectors it claims plus an explicit skip list, instead of N-1/N with a paragraph — the number stops depending on prose.
mapping_guard_note: The `decline` kind strings are KISS's vocabulary. KISS enforces their exhaustiveness at generation time (a new KeyDecline variant is a build error) — that protects only the KISS side. A consumer mapping these onto its own decline enum MUST guard the mapping itself; a variant added on either side silently staleness the table.
coverage_note: The positive vectors exercise the structure_key token GRAMMAR — field order, optional-field presence, sentinel spellings, work-class/dispatch, and decline verdicts — NOT the dtype vocabulary: they place only a few of the 22 usable dtypes in the dtype position, so a dtype-spelling divergence on a token that never appears is invisible to a byte-match against this set. Vocabulary agreement is a DIFFERENT instrument's job and IS closed there: the dtype-manifest gate — tools/test_kiss_dtypes_manifest.py, over conformance/corpus/dtype_manifest.json — asserts each dtype token's metadata, so a c128->c127 respell raises there, naming the token. Nor do the POSITIVE vectors test decline-side rules: rule (d) — rejecting the all-default redundant (acc+mp) form — is exercised only by the decline vector 'redundant_acc_mp_all_default' -> RedundantAccMpField (a deriver covers it by running the DECLINE vectors on the parse side, or by proving the redundant form unconstructible on the emit side; never by the positive byte-match). So 'the byte-match passed' means the token grammar agrees; the vocabulary is confirmed by the manifest and the decline-side rules by the decline vectors, not by this positive set. Three further blind spots, each with a DIFFERENT remedy so a reader knows what to do next: (c) the positives are a SAMPLE, not a census — a divergence that surfaces as a DIFFERENT cell (a shape this set never places) rather than a different spelling of the SAME cell is invisible, and is closed by sampling more cells, never by this set agreeing. (d) op-family ASSIGNMENT is upstream of the token — the op_family code is IN each token, but which concrete op maps to which §6.5-0006 family is the consumer's CLASSIFICATION, made before any token exists, so a party that files an op under the wrong family emits a token for a different cell (absent here), not a mismatched spelling of this one; a category error no token-level check can see, closed only by a classification instrument. [(c) and (d) share a shape — the byte-match tests spelling agreement on the cells sampled, not which cells EXIST or how ops MAP — but NOT a remedy, so they are named separately: (c) is a coverage gap, (d) is a category gap.] (e) Agreement on a PASS-THROUGH field is not evidence of independent DERIVATION of it. (Whether umbrella §5.3's implementation count should instead be per-FIELD is #208's OPEN question, owned there; this note claims only what THIS positive set cannot see.) A field a consumer carries VERBATIM (copied from a shared source, not derived from its own graph) byte-matches across every party sharing that source whether or not any DERIVED it and whether or not it is CORRECT. The lone pass-through field here is the `target` capability token's namespace-owned capability-SET SUFFIX — the part AFTER the colon (the namespace PREFIX `cuda`/`vulkan` is ThinkersJournal-registry-owned under §6.8 and IS checked; only the suffix is the maintainer's vocabulary). It is carried OPAQUELY by every consumer that compares it, and NONE derives it; one such `vulkan:` suffix once byte-matched green while it was MALFORMED against vulkan v4 — that incident is the proof this positive set cannot see the field. TWO DIFFERENT #200 instruments cover it, and they are not one: (i) the `namespace_vocabulary_versions` STAMP records which vocabulary version each embedded suffix was generated against — it proves BINDING, not CURRENCY: a stamp cannot report whether that vocabulary has SINCE moved, only which one was used, so detecting a STALE suffix needs a party comparing the stamp against the live namespace document (the §6.8-0008 manifest is that comparator, the sibling of the dtype-manifest gate above). The stamp alone is genuinely WEAKER than the arity gate; and (ii) the generation-time ARITY GATE refuses to emit a suffix whose FIELD COUNT violates the recorded arity, making a WRONG-ARITY suffix UNPUBLISHABLE — the instrument that closed the vulkan incident, which was an arity break. It counts `.`-separated fields only; it does NOT validate field CONTENT against the vocabulary, so a suffix with the right field count but a wrong field value (an unknown `ops-…` code, say) passes the gate and is caught by the namespace-vocabulary manifest (§6.8-0008), not here. The arity gate is also a TWO-LINK guarantee, not one: the generator cannot emit a token that violates the IN-CODE arity, and the in-code arity cannot drift from `spec/namespaces/<ns>.md` WHILE ITS BINDING TEST RUNS (arity is pinned in code and bound to the document by test — deliberately, to keep the emitter pure and the artifact path-independent). None of this is confirmed by this positive byte-match.
